summary.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA margin rose to 17.91% (from 5.33%) on operating income of ₹186.08 crore, up 21.16% YoY.
summary.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA improved 2.85x to ₹33.32 crore, with margin up 1258 bps to 17.91%. PAT before exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (2.04x YoY), a 13.26% margin. Management said three CDMO partnerships (Viatris, Manx UK, Arrotex Australia) were commercialised in the quarter, with only ₹5-6 crore booked from the Viatris products so far. Management guided to 18%+ sustainable EBITDA margin, a ₹900 crore revenue target for FY27, and ₹1,200 crore by FY29, with ₹250 crore of cash to be deployed in capex over about 2.5 years.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales, up from 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites own-brand mix as the main driver of margin expansion.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales, down from 29% in Q1 FY26. Viatris products (Ibuprofen, Clarithromycin granules) contributed only ₹5-6 crore in the quarter.

segments.name: Domestic (branded generics, ethical, CMO)
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41% (vs 10%), ethical 6.14% (vs 7%), domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% (vs 6%) of Q1 FY27 sales.

segments.name: Product portfolio (FY26)
segments.commentary: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore (from ₹47.96 crore); Ezetimibe+Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore (+246.97%); Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore (vs ₹79.67 crore); Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore and Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore, both roughly doubled.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO; management also cited ₹900 crore revenue for FY27.
Revenue target of ₹1,200 crore by FY29 retained; management said it would revisit numbers at year-end, not now.
Viatris CDMO products expected to contribute ₹200-220 crore incremental revenue in FY27 (management later said ₹100-130 crore from the two Viatris molecules, ramping over about two years).
EBITDA margin expected to exceed 18%, with management targeting Q3 FY27 for a move above 20% and possibly 21-22% if quarter-on-quarter sales grow.
Medium-term growth target of 20-25% CAGR with EBITDA margin above 18%, confirmed on the call.
FY30 aspiration: revenue of at least ₹1,500 crore and net profit of about ₹200 crore plus.
Dossiers to rise from 2,100+ to 2,500 by Q4 FY27 (management said 400+ additions).
capex_capacity: Capex of about ₹250 crore to be deployed over about 2-2.5 years, covering a new warehouse near the factory, capacity enhancement at the existing facility and the Jammu facility.
Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards under way; Jammu facility being audited for PIC/S and EU.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules was about 70% in Q1 (pilot batches included); management expects 90% utilisation of planned capacity over time.
Expansion for an additional CDMO project: capex of ₹50-75 crore for revenue of ₹150+ crore, if two prospective customers sign.
New R&D facility: land bought at Panchkula. R&D is working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex will start only after filings.
demand_pricing: Viatris paid about USD 2 million for development work, to be reimbursed through orders; management said no spend was made until agreements were signed.

Management cited a minimum 50-55% gross margin threshold for new products; Ezetimibe+Atorvastatin is supplied to Tiffen-Becker, with Ind-Swift earning 50% of the profit above transfer price (43% quoted).
Export gross margin cited as about 55% by management; domestic gross margins quoted by an analyst at 76% (ethical), 51% (own-brand), 42% (CMO).
Management said export sales have no seasonality; domestic sales are somewhat seasonal.
Q2 FY27 expected to see Arrotex push on Macrogol; Q3-Q4 to see Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules; Viatris volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What was the CDMO contribution this quarter and expected growth over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Only ₹5-6 crore from the Viatris molecules (Ibuprofen, Clarithromycin granules) in Q1; ₹100-130 crore is expected from these two over about two years, not ₹200 crore in year one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for ₹250 crore cash and the Synthimed stake?
qa_highlights.answer: The cash will be deployed in capex over about 2.5 years; no Synthimed divestment is planned this year, and its FY27 budgeted EBITDA is about ₹750 crore. Management said Q1 results were on track.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% margin sustainable and can it rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is sustainable and could reach 21-22% with quarter-on-quarter sales growth; Q3 FY27 is the target to move above 18%, with Q2 possible internally.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D was retained?
qa_highlights.answer: The API business was sold in FY24 to Synthimed for net approx ₹2,000-2,100 crore, used to repay about ₹1,250-1,300 crore of group debt. Retained R&D in Panchkula handles regulatory, tech transfer and filings, with new land bought for a facility.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 ₹1,200 crore guidance seen as conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not revise now, may revisit after FY27 overachievement, and said the target depends on capacity expansion and revenue-linked drivers.

qa_highlights.question: What were the capacity utilisation and dossier targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules was about 70%, with the annual figure computed only yearly. Dossiers are expected to reach 2,500 by Q4 FY27 from 2,100+.

risks_watch: Viatris and new CDMO ramp is back-ended: Q1 contribution was only ₹5-6 crore against ₹200-220 crore FY27 expectation.
Management says new CDMO partnerships are slowed by the war and will not come this year; the ₹1,200 crore FY29 target depends on capacity expansion.
Synthimed stake (about 7.8%) is held with a tag-along right; the private equity partner may exit after about five years.
Ezetimibe+Atorvastatin economics depend on a transfer-price arrangement with Tiffen-Becker.
Management could not give Q1 capacity utilisation or addressable market size on the call; these are to follow.
Watch Q2 FY27 for Arrotex Macrogol and Viatris volume growth, and Q3 for EBITDA margin above 20%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the growth roadmap, with management repeatedly saying targets could be beaten. Cautious and evasive on specifics: it deferred capacity utilisation, addressable market size, product names for new CDMO customers and any FY29 target revision.
key_quotes: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.
So the day we committed for Viatris we delivered.
We don't want to overproject and want to say that we'll do this one year in advance.

adds.what: New warehouse near the factory (part of ₹250 cr capex plan)
Capacity enhancement at existing facility (part of ₹250 cr capex plan)
Jammu facility expansion (part of ₹250 cr capex plan; PIC/S and EU audit under way)
Additional CDMO project capacity: ₹50-75 cr capex for ₹150+ cr revenue, contingent on two prospective customers signing

growth.why: Management guides ~₹900 cr FY27 revenue (vs ~₹750 cr export target at 45% CDMO) and ₹1,200 cr by FY29, backed by ₹200-220 cr incremental Viatris/Manx/Arrotex CDMO revenue in FY27 and ₹250 cr capex over ~2-2.5 years, but capacity is at ~70% utilisation and the capex timing is 4+ quarters out with no sized, signed capacity for the ₹900 cr target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin at 17.91% in Q1 FY27 vs 5.33% a year ago; management guides above 18% sustainable and above 20% by Q3 FY27, with 21-22% possible if sales grow QoQ, driven by own-brand export mix (57.20% of sales vs 48%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ₹250 cr capex over ~2-2.5 years covers warehouse, existing-facility capacity enhancement and Jammu, but no dated commissioning was given and Q1 utilisation was ~70%, so new capacity is planned yet not firmly dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Arrotex Macrogol push in Q2, Viatris volumes to double in Q2 vs Q1, and Ibuprofen/granules ramp in Q3-Q4, against only ₹5-6 cr Viatris revenue in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only ~70% so a large new plant is not forced, but ₹250 cr capex is already guided and a ₹50-75 cr additional CDMO expansion (₹62.5 cr midpoint) is approved pending two customer signings.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says targets could be beaten and will revisit the ₹1,200 cr FY29 target after FY27 overachievement, but guided ~₹900 cr FY27 revenue only as a target with Viatris ramp back-ended.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Viatris CDMO contribution was ₹5-6 cr in Q1 against ₹200-220 cr FY27 expectation (later ₹100-130 cr over two years), and new CDMO partnerships are slowed by the war with none expected this year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules (Viatris) are slated for Q3-Q4 FY27, and R&D is working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29, though filings must come first.

rows.label: Viatris CDMO ramp (two molecules)
rows.why: Management guides ₹100-130 cr from the two Viatris molecules over ~2 years, with volumes expected to double in Q2 from ₹5-6 cr in Q1.

rows.label: Dossier additions to 2,500 by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Dossiers rising from 2,100+ with 400+ additions guided, supporting regulatory filings for new CDMO and export products.

rows.label: Samba EU-GMP/PIC-S upgrade and Jammu audit
rows.why: Samba upgrade is under way and Jammu is being audited for PIC/S and EU, which would open regulated markets but no completion date was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins (18% sustainable, >20% by Q3 FY27) and on beating targets, but cautious and evasive on CDMO timing, utilisation, addressable market and any FY29 revision; analysts pushed on the back-ended Viatris ramp and the ₹1,200 cr FY29 target.
